summary: Franklin County observer post: 1921 Aermotor LS40 tower, closed 1970, removed 1977; the summit is a public hike with a memorial and no tower.

facts.design: Aermotor LS40 steel tower on four-leg truss construction
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1977; the summit has bare rock and a memorial, no tower.

access.note: Trail from a trailhead on NY 3 to the summit, on state land in the High Peaks Wilderness; very popular, and the parking area often overflows.

visit.trail_note: Short, steep hike from the NY 3 trailhead; there is no tower to climb.

facts.agency: New York State Conservation Commission, later the Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Observation station established in August 1911; no tower at first, and the observer's first structure was a stone hut
A 22-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower was purchased and erected
Observer Walter C. Rice gave up the post because of his health
A new observer's cabin was built to the 1928 standard design
A bear attacked a state observer as he walked down from the tower; he was treated and went home
Closed at the end of the 1970 season as aerial detection took over
Removed in August 1977; Wikipedia gives July

corrections.why: Three sources give the tower as 22 ft (6.7 m), and Wikipedia gives 6.7 m. The 15.2 m (about 50 ft) figure matches only the 1942 survey description. Editor to confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Most sources give 22 ft (6.7 m); the 1942 Coast and Geodetic Survey description says about 50 ft. The story reports both. Proposed record value is 6.7 m, pending editor review.
The Forest Lookouts page says August 1977; Wikipedia says July 1977. The story says 1977 and notes both.
A June 1922 newspaper says he had to give up the post that year; Wikipedia and a 2022 blog say he manned the tower until 1923.

notes_for_editor: Built 1921, closed 1970 and removed 1977 are well supported. Record height 15.2 m conflicts with 22 ft in most sources; see corrections. Access changed from unknown to public (summit trail on state land). No source describes whether the tower footings survive; the 1942 survey point sat at the centre of the tower base. The 2022 blog says the memorial dates Rice to 1915-1923, which conflicts with the 1922 newspaper.
